key_insight: TipSweep transfers the optimal learning rate across trainable block counts, with approximate scaling of k⁻¹ for FP32 master weights and k⁻¹ᐟ² for direct BF16 updates.
engineering_relevance: Searching learning rates on only the last transformer block can reduce post-training tuning costs before scaling to more blocks or the full model.
method: Search candidate learning rates while training only the last k₀ blocks, typically k₀ = 1.
Transfer the selected rate to k trainable blocks using precision-dependent scaling rules.
Explain the scaling with an analytical model that accounts for update rounding.
evidence_signal: Experiments span 1–7B-parameter models; for a 6.7B model, separate prototypes fit search within 16 GiB GPU memory and evaluate five candidates using about half the GPU-hours of one full-depth run.
watch_item: The scaling rules are approximate and depend on whether updates use FP32 master weights or directly modify BF16 weights.
paper_title: Precision-Aware Learning Rate Transfer Across Block Count in LLM Post-Training
